rules: Maps are spatial data first and presentation second.
Every landmark has coordinates and a scale.
Higher-detail maps inherit lower-scale coordinates instead of inventing disconnected geography.
Stone establishes terrain mass; lichen, water and vegetation are derived layers.
Paths connect places and may become narrative routes.
Memory records changes without rewriting the underlying coordinate geometry.
